evidence.quote: {{root|en|ine-pro|*mews-|id=moss}} The {{glossary|adjective}} is derived from Late {{inh|en|enm|musty}}; further origin {{uncertain|en|nocap=1}}, possibly from one of the following:<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=''adj.''{{sup|2}}|noformat=1|id=124278|date=June 2022|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|pos=adj}}</ref> * From {{der|en|xno|muste}}, {{m|xno|moste}}, variants of {{m|xno|moiste}}, {{m|xno|muiste|t=moist}}, from {{der|en|fro|moiste|t=clammy, damp, moist, wet}} (modern {{cog|fr|moite|t=muggy; sticky, sweaty}}), from a {{glossary|blend}} of {{der|en|la-vul|*mucidus}} (from {{der|en|la|mūcidus|t=mouldy, musty}}, from Old {{der|en|la|mūceō|t=to be mouldy or musty}} + {{m|la|-idus|pos={{glossary|suffix}} mea
"moldy, sour," perhaps a variant of moisty "moist, damp" (see moist), but musty, of… See origin and meaning of musty. from Old French moiste "damp, wet, soaked" (13c.
